- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is falling.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 2–5 day lag correction: if price spiked 3+ days ago, reduce forecast by 2–5%.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 75% above 18d mean, cap at 1.5x mean; if < 75% below, don’t force correction.  
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle; reduce first 5–7 days by 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, assume no directional bias; apply only mean reversion and lag corrections.
